extracted.intended_audience: Potential intervenors, protesters, applicants, and members of the public participating in FERC proceedings (e.g., parties considering intervention or protest in Docket No. ER24-2394)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural guidance for filing motions to intervene or protests in a Federal Energy Regulatory Commission docket, including deadlines, service, electronic filing, and public-access instructions. Focused on participation in the listed market-based rate/blanket authorization proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: File in accordance with Rules 211 and 214 (18 CFR 385.211 and 385.214)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person desiring to intervene or to protest should file with the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission ... in accordance with Rules 211 and 214 of the Commission's Rules of Practice and Procedure (18 CFR 385.211 and 385.214).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing must comply with the procedural requirements set out in those rules (timing, content, format as applicable).

rubrics_metrics.name: Service on the Applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: Anyone filing a motion to intervene or protest must serve a copy of that document on the Applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure timely service of the protest/intervention filing on the Applicant as part of compliance with the filing rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness — Deadline for protests
rubrics_metrics.description: Notice is hereby given that the deadline for filing protests with regard to the applicant's request for blanket authorization ... is July 25, 2024.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protests received after this date may be untimely; confirm the relevant deadline for the specific issue (here, protests relating to the blanket authorization request).

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject of protests — blanket authorization under 18 CFR part 34
rubrics_metrics.description: This is a supplemental notice ... noting that such application includes a request for blanket authorization, under 18 CFR part 34, of future issuances of securities and assumptions of liability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protests should be specific to the applicant's request for blanket authorization under 18 CFR part 34 (future issuances of securities and assumptions of liability).

rubrics_metrics.name: Encouraged electronic submission via FERC Online
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission encourages electronic submission of protests and interventions in lieu of paper, using the FERC Online links at www.ferc.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To facilitate electronic service, persons with internet access who will eFile a document and/or be listed as a contact for an intervenor must create and validate an eRegistration account using the eRegistration link, and select the eFiling link to log on and submit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative: mail or hand-delivery if unable to eFile
rubrics_metrics.description: Persons unable to file electronically may mail similar pleadings to the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission, 888 First Street NE, Washington, DC 20426. Hand delivered submissions in docketed proceedings should be delivered to Health and Human Services, 12225 Wilkins Avenue, Rockville, Maryland 20852.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the stated mailing address for mailed pleadings; follow the hand-delivery instructions and address if physically delivering documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public access via Commission Home Page / eLibrary
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission provides all interested persons an opportunity to view and/or print the contents of this document via the internet through the Commission's Home Page (http://www.ferc.gov). From the Commission's Home Page ... this information is available on eLibrary. The full text of this document is available on eLibrary in PDF and Microsoft Word format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To access this document in eLibrary, type the docket number excluding the last three digits of this document in the docket number field; documents are available for viewing, printing, and downloading.

rubrics_metrics.name: User assistance contacts for eLibrary and FERC website
rubrics_metrics.description: User assistance is available for eLibrary and the Commission's website during normal business hours from FERC Online Support at 202-502-6652 (toll free at 1-866-208-3676) or email at ferconlinesupport@ferc.gov, or the Public Reference Room at (202) 502-8371, TTY (202) 502-8659. Email the Public Reference Room at public.referenceroom@ferc.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact these numbers/emails for help accessing documents or using FERC online services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office of Public Participation (OPP) support for meaningful engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission's Office of Public Participation (OPP) supports meaningful public engagement and participation in Commission proceedings. OPP can help members of the public, including landowners, environmental justice communities, Tribal members and others, access publicly available information and navigate Commission processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For public inquiries and assistance with making filings such as interventions, comments, or requests for rehearing, contact OPP at (202) 502-6595 or OPP@ferc.gov.

rubrics_metrics.name: Officialness and verification of FederalRegister.gov XML rendition
rubrics_metrics.description: This site displays a prototype of a “Web 2.0” version of the daily Federal Register. It is not an official legal edition of the Federal Register ... those relying on it for legal research should verify their results against an official edition of the Federal Register. Until the ACFR grants it official status, the XML rendition of the daily Federal Register on FederalRegister.gov does not provide legal notice to the public or judicial notice to the courts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the linked PDF on govinfo.gov or the official print/electronic editions for legal notice; verify content against official sources when conducting legal research or meeting filing deadlines.
